FOR YOU

Your care team is planning how to feed your baby through a feeding tube. One common check is to measure any milk left in the baby's stomach (called a gastric residual). The team is still deciding whether to do these checks.

The evidence is very uncertain about whether checking stomach residuals regularly makes it take longer before your baby can reach full feeds, compared with not checking them. This is in very low birth weight babies. There is very little confidence in this finding, and it may not apply to your baby.

Your baby's team will look at things like your baby's gestational age, birth weight, and how well they are tolerating feeds. They will also look at signs such as tummy swelling, vomiting, green or bilious fluid, or concerns about blood flow. These signs can be a reason to check residuals even though it is very uncertain whether checking slows feeds. The team will keep reviewing the feeding plan and change it if feeds are taking longer than expected.

If you have questions about your baby's feeding plan, please ask your care team. This note does not replace their clinical judgement.

Claim: The evidence is very uncertain about whether routine gastric residual monitoring is associated with a longer time to full enteral feeds than no monitoring.
